FR-001.title: The system MUST provide a read-only health check that can be run against any spec directory at any time and MUST NOT modify any file it inspects.

FR-002.title: The health check MUST produce a meaningful verdict for a spec created before this feature existed, deriving its findings from the run record and the on-disk files alone.

FR-003.title: The health check MUST report any step whose start has no matching finish, naming the step.

FR-004.title: The health check MUST report any task marked done in the task list that has no matching finish in the run record.

FR-005.title: The health check MUST detect task finishes clustered into a single burst and report them as batched journaling rather than as measured per-task durations.

FR-006.title: The health check MUST report attribution anomalies — a step closed by an author that is not the one the pipeline reserves for that step.

FR-007.title: The health check MUST classify the "status says one thing, the pipeline bar offers another" symptom as either "the records disagree with each other" (a capture defect) or "the records are consistent" (a display defect).

FR-008.title: The health check MUST state which checks it ran and which it could not run, and MUST NOT report a clean verdict for checks it skipped.

FR-009.title: The health check MUST exit successfully whatever it finds; a finding is a report, never a gate that blocks a pipeline.

FR-010.title: The capture runtime MUST record one trace entry for every call it handles, including calls that fail, without requiring any additional call from the run.

FR-011.title: A failed capture call MUST leave a trace entry carrying the reason it failed.

FR-012.title: The trace MUST be stored locally per spec, excluded from version control, and capped in size so it cannot grow without bound.

FR-013.title: Writing a trace entry MUST NOT measurably slow a run and MUST NOT add any instruction text to a command body.

FR-014.title: The health check MUST consume the trace to report call counts, failure counts, payload sizes, loaded-context sizes, and per-file rewrite counts.

FR-015.title: The drift audit MUST recompute drift itself from the deterministic ground truth and MUST NOT trust any previously recorded drift verdict.

FR-016.title: The drift audit MUST show its work for each flag: the capability, the files changed since that capability's spec was last committed, and the commits that changed them.

FR-017.title: The drift audit MUST classify each flag as real drift, self-inflicted (caused by the companion's own writes), or suspect baseline (wrong comparison point, renames).

FR-018.title: The drift audit MUST report a recorded claim of drift-clean that contradicts its own recomputation as a false claim.

FR-019.title: The drift audit MUST report a capability whose baseline cannot be determined as unknown with the reason, never as clean.

FR-020.title: Drift evaluations MUST record their own inputs to the trace so repeated verdicts can be compared over time.

FR-021.title: When completion was attempted but the spec did not reach the terminal state, the health check MUST state which of these happened: the write never arrived, the write was refused (and why), or the write landed and the display disagrees.

FR-022.title: The health check MUST distinguish "completion was never attempted" from "completion failed".

FR-023.title: The health check MUST verify the task list still carries its generated shape — one phase per user story, waves inside each phase, join lines and checkpoints intact.

FR-024.title: The health check MUST flag a task list whose user-story sections were renamed, flattened, or replaced after generation as a template violation, naming the offending headings.

FR-025.title: The system MUST provide a debug switch in the project's own companion configuration file, not as an editor setting.

FR-026.title: When the debug switch is off, command bodies MUST contain no instrumentation text at all — absent, not dormant.

FR-027.title: When the debug switch is on, re-rendered command bodies MUST carry step-by-step timing instrumentation that yields per-step timing on the next run.

FR-028.title: A change to the debug switch MUST affect the next dispatched command and MUST NOT alter a command already in flight.

FR-029.title: The health check MUST offer an optional deep audit that reads the AI session transcript covering the run's time window.

FR-030.title: The deep audit MUST distinguish work that was tried and failed, work that was retried, and work that was never attempted.

FR-031.title: The deep audit MUST surface claims recorded during the run that contradict the recomputed reality.

FR-032.title: The deep audit MUST quantify wasted output, including extra summaries, narration, and repeated rewrites of the same file.

FR-033.title: The deep audit MUST degrade to a single "not available" line and exit successfully where no transcript exists or its format can no longer be parsed.

FR-034.title: The measurement harness MUST produce a trace for runs performed in its comparison folders and MUST fold the health check's verdict into its scoring.

FR-035.title: The harness MUST include a deliberately oversized variant large enough to surface batched task journaling when it occurs.

FR-036.title: The harness MUST include a failure-injection fixture that proves a failed capture is recorded and reported rather than lost.

FR-037.title: Existing capture, drift, and completion behavior MUST be unchanged for a user who never runs the health check and never turns debug on.

FR-038.title: Every part of this feature MUST inherit the runtime's never-fail-the-host contract: a missing interpreter, an unreadable file, or an unresolvable directory reports the problem and continues, never halting the pipeline.

FR-039.title: The closing of a task SHOULD be reducible to a single call rather than the current pair of calls, without changing what is recorded.

FR-040.title: The end-of-step capture calls SHOULD be reducible to a single batched call rather than a volley of separate calls, without changing what is recorded.

FR-041.title: The health check MUST report a specification that carries planning or tasking content — a task checklist, or a file-by-file breakdown — and name the evidence it found.

FR-042.title: The health check MUST report a plan document that carries a task checklist as planning having done tasking work.

FR-043.title: The health check MUST report a task list that carries substantial implementation code as tasking having done implementation work.

FR-044.title: The health check MUST report the same task identifiers appearing in more than one artifact, naming the artifacts.

FR-045.title: The health check MUST report source files committed while the run was still in a step before implement, naming the files and their commits.

FR-046.title: The health check MUST report a step before implement that consumed a larger share of the run than implement itself, as a signal rather than as a defect.

FR-047.title: The health check MUST NOT report a deliberately fast-tracked small change as bleed when its specification carries its approach inline and its plan is a pointer.

context: area: speckit-extension/scripts — write-context.py, drift.py, companion_config.py, build-commands.py
area: speckit-extension/nodes + commands — bodies are generated, never hand-edited
area: examples/todo-claude/bench — harness variants and scoring
constraint: recording MUST NOT be able to break the run it observes (never-fail-the-host)
constraint: a probe that cannot determine an answer reports unknown, never the negative
constraint: a report MUST NOT claim success for work it did not do
constraint: command bodies are assembled from single-sourced parts/nodes and gated byte-identical
constraint: source of truth is speckit-extension/, not the installed .specify/extensions/companion copy
intent: Give every Companion run a free self-record, plus a read-only health check that recomputes reality instead of trusting claims, and a debug switch that only costs something while it is on.
expectations: The health check reports only — it never repairs a finding, and never gates or blocks a pipeline
No change to capture, drift, or completion behavior for users who never run the health check or enable debug
The trace is a local, gitignored diagnostic — never uploaded, never committed, no telemetry contract
The deep transcript audit is a builder's tool, not a supported product surface; transcript format is not a stable contract
No new VS Code setting — the debug switch lives in the project's own companion configuration file
Command bodies are not hand-edited; instrumentation arrives only through the existing assembly pipeline
approach: Wire a tiny append-only tracer into the single funnel write-context.py and drift.py already have, so every call — including the early returns that currently vanish into stderr — leaves a line. Add a read-only doctor command backed by focused check modules that read the run record, the on-disk artifacts, and that trace, and that shells out to drift.py as ground truth rather than reimplementing drift. Deliver debug mode by appending a debug-timing part through the same conditional seam assemble-nodes.py already uses for the orchestrator part, so an off render carries no instrumentation text at all.

decisions.decision: Trace by wrapping main() in write-context.py and compute_drift() in drift.py
decisions.why: Both scripts funnel every path through one entry point and return 0 on failure by design, so the funnel is the only placement that catches the early returns — unresolvable feature dir, refused lifecycle key, feature-dir/tasks-file mismatch — which are exactly the failures that vanish today
decisions.rejected: Decorating each capture writer, which would only trace calls that got far enough to reach a writer

decisions.decision: The trace file self-ignores by writing specs/NNN/.gitignore on first write
decisions.why: The trace must be gitignored in every project that installs the extension, and a capture call cannot edit a users root .gitignore as a side effect; a self-ignoring sibling is one idempotent write needing no user action and no installer step
decisions.rejected: A system temp directory (the trace must survive the run and be findable days later) and an install-time ignore rule (would not cover specs created by a project that installed earlier)

decisions.decision: The drift audit shells out to drift.py --json as ground truth
decisions.why: compute_drift is already the deterministic authority and already separates tracked from unspeced and reports skips with reasons; reimplementing it would create the second source of truth this feature exists to eliminate, and running it as a user would also exercises its entry point
decisions.rejected: Reimplementing drift inside the doctor, and importing compute_drift directly (materially the same but bypasses the entry point)

decisions.decision: Classify drift flags as real, self-inflicted, suspect-baseline, or unknown
decisions.why: These are the two false-alarm shapes the issue names and both are decidable from what git already knows; keeping unknown distinct from real and from clean is required by the capture runtimes own rule that a probe which cannot determine an answer never returns the negative
decisions.rejected: A confidence score, which invites the same is-it-real shrug the current warning already produces

decisions.decision: Decide the status-vs-display triage from status-context.py against derive-from-files.py plus a Python re-derivation of the step badges
decisions.why: The viewer derives its stepper badges from history[] alone with no file-existence fallback, so status says specified but no Plan button is almost always a history[] gap; deciding from the readings the system already computes is what makes the verdict trustworthy
decisions.rejected: Reading the TypeScript derivation through a Node shim — the doctor must run in a repo with no Node toolchain

decisions.decision: Debug mode appends a debug-timing part through the existing conditional-append seam
decisions.why: Reusing the orchestrator seam means no new mechanism for changing command text, which the companion-commands living spec requires, and appending rather than toggling is what makes an off render contain no instrumentation text at all
decisions.rejected: A conditional block inside each node body (present-but-dormant, and duplicated five times) and a recipe node-order swap (a recipe replaces the whole order, so a project using both would lose one)

decisions.decision: Keep --append and --materialize and add --close-task rather than replacing them
decisions.why: The two-call shape exists because parallel workers must append without contending while only the main agent may fold; the merge removes the main agents redundant second call for its own task, not the ability to do them separately
decisions.rejected: Replacing the two flags outright, which would let a fanned-out worker put a second writer on the shared record

decisions.decision: Ship the doctor as a command with no VS Code panel
decisions.why: It must run on a repo with no VS Code session, retroactively on old specs, and headlessly inside the bench; a panel would also put the diagnosis behind the very display the doctor exists to put on trial
decisions.rejected: Shipping a panel first — deferred to a follow-up once the verdict shape has settled

plan.summary: Five new modules plus a debug part in speckit-extension/, all stdlib Python, hanging off seams that already exist — no new mechanism anywhere.
plan.key_finding: The viewer derives its stepper badges from history[] alone with no file-existence fallback, so the reported specified-but-no-Plan-button symptom is a history[] gap in almost every case — which is what makes the status-vs-display triage decidable from two readings the codebase already computes.
plan.risks: The --chat audit rides on a transcript format with no compatibility promise; it is quarantined in its own module and documented as a builders tool for that reason.

tasks.summary: 55 tasks across 11 phases — Setup, Foundational, one phase per user story (US1–US8), and Polish; every phase laid out as waves with explicit join lines, and all 40 requirements mapped to tasks.
